clue.text: American informed about criminal wrongdoing, it follows

indicators.note: the word for informed goes about, that is around, the rest of the pieces

parts.note: someone wise is informed or knowing

indicators.note: follows places the word it after the wrongdoing

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A US citizen, tipped off about some crime, follows up the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like an adjective for wrongdoing, but it is a noun of its own, a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the state of Wisconsin is, by nationality, an American.

clue.text: Mother saw potty on top of that

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters of these two words go mad and rearrange

explanation.surface: Mum caught sight of the potty, perched on top of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' reads as a child's toilet, but it is the anagram signal, in its sense of crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms adding a further point to an argument: furthermore, besides.

clue.text: Ripe cheese men found under small container

indicators.note: in a down entry, pieces found under others come after them

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tin is a container
in chess the pieces are called men

explanation.surface: Some smelly cheese turns up beneath a little box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' gives two chessmen at once, king and bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinking Bishop is a pungent washed-rind English cheese, famously strong-smelling, so ripe in both senses.

clue.text: My tough love has inspired hatred primarily on the climb

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading the letters from bottom to top, so backwards
to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: a yob is a tough, a thug
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letter of the word hatred

explanation.surface: A tough-love regime breeds hatred as one scales the heights.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes into YOBO, giving YOBHO, which is turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or excitement, as in 'My, what a view!'

clue.text: Sweet biscuit or taco oddly dunked in drink

indicators.note: a biscuit dunked in a drink sits inside it, so these letters go inside the drink

parts.note: a shake, or milkshake, is a drink

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of taco, its first and third

explanation.surface: A choice of biscuit or taco, both dipped in a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a link offering a choice; it is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortcake is a crumbly, buttery biscuit or cake eaten as a sweet treat.

clue.text: Oppose sound of horse, perhaps

indicators.note: sound of tells us to hear the horse's call spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a horse's call is a neigh
say means perhaps or for instance, as in 'say, ten of them'

explanation.surface: A query whether a whinny might be the noise a horse makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To naysay is to refuse, deny or speak against something, so to oppose it.

clue.text: Error mine, ultimately? That's rich!

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law, an error of conduct

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the final letter of the word mine

explanation.surface: Someone admits the mistake was finally theirs, and a listener retorts sarcastically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's rich!' sounds like an indignant retort; it is the definition, describing a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich, dense, many-layered cake, so the exclamation fairly describes one.

clue.text: See 2
By the sound of it, tool fixed

indicators.note: this phrase says the tool's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a spade is a digging tool

explanation.surface: Listening to it, the tool seems to have been repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed' suggests repaired; here it is the vet's euphemism for neutered.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed is a euphemism for neutered, and a spayed female animal has had her ovaries removed.

clue.text: Asian queen in India, offensive briefly

parts.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the queen goes in among the other letters
briefly cuts the last letter off the word for an offensive

parts.note: a raid is a military offensive
Q is the abbreviation for queen, as in chess

explanation.surface: A queen visiting India makes a short attack.
explanation.walkthrough: I plus RAI (RAID cut short) takes Q inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq lies in western Asia, so a person from Iraq is an Asian.

clue.text: Mine is gathering fluff when viewed in the mirror

indicators.note: a mirror image reads backwards, so these letters run in reverse

parts.note: a party is a social gathering
to fluff is to botch, and a boob is a blunder

explanation.surface: Someone's looking in the mirror and finding their own fluff.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine is an explosive device, and a booby trap is a hidden device triggered by an unwitting victim.

clue.text: Chief on drugs finding something on computer

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: hash is short for hashish, a drug
key means chief or principal, as in a key figure

explanation.surface: A boss on narcotics stumbles on something on a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: The hash key, marked #, is a key found on a computer keyboard.

clue.text: Grizzly caught by shot, calamity!

indicators.note: one piece is caught by another, held inside it

parts.note: a shot is an attempt, a try
grizzly means grey-haired, so old or aged

explanation.surface: A bear is bagged by a hunter's shot, a disaster for the bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grizzly' looks like the bear; it is the adjective meaning grey-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a disastrous event, a calamity.

clue.text: Remarkably, half of people in China related to an ancient civilisation

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something unusual, so these letters are rearranged in an unusual order
half of takes the first three of the six letters of people

explanation.surface: Remarkably, half the population of China is linked to some ancient culture.
explanation.walkthrough: PEO plus IN CHINA is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenicia was an ancient seafaring civilisation of the Levant, and Phoenician is its adjective.

clue.text: Bubbling up by river in African country, is maelstrom

indicators.note: the reversed letters go in the country's name

parts.note: Chad is a country in central Africa

indicators.note: in a down entry, bubbling up means rising from bottom to top, so the letters read backwards

explanation.surface: Water bubbles up beside a river in Africa, making a whirlpool.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Charybdis was a deadly whirlpool opposite Scylla, so a byword for a maelstrom.

clue.text: Surrounded by four characters in crowd, I marched back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
four characters in says four letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A marcher recalls being in the thick of the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'four characters in' unassigned; it is the hiding indicator. DIMA, in crowD I MArched, reads back.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning in the middle of, surrounded by.

clue.text: Without competition, unable to compete?

definitions.meaning: unrivalled, having no equal or competitor
read literally, ... means lacking a match, so having no game to play in

explanation.surface: Being peerless means there is nobody left to play against.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchless means incomparable, while literally it means having no match or contest to enter.

clue.text: Plastic upper-class snubbed by Azeri nobility?

indicators.note: to be snubbed is to be shut out, so the letter is left out of the phrase

parts.note: Baku is the capital of Azerbaijan, so it stands in for things Azeri
U is the abbreviation for upper-class, as in U and non-U
the elite are the nobility, the upper crust

explanation.surface: The posh are cold-shouldered by Azerbaijan's aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: '?' flags the playful Baku elite for Azeri nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakelite was an early synthetic resin, one of the first commercial plastics.

clue.text: See 21
Rich heiress in sports car, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks us to hear the word spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a Porsche is a German sports car

explanation.surface: A wealthy heiress driving a fancy car, or so the speaker heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Portia, in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, is the wealthy heiress of Belmont.

clue.text: Outlaw Y chromosome?

definitions.meaning: the Y chromosome is the factor that makes an embryo male

explanation.surface: A query whether the Y chromosome is what makes a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a criminal, while split as male factor it describes the sex-determining chromosome.

clue.text: Slight offensive to me, rebuff not entirely uplifting

indicators.note: in a down entry, uplifting raises the letters so they read bottom to top, backwards
not entirely means only part of these words is used, letters lying within them

explanation.surface: A minor attack hurts, though the snub is not wholly crushing.
explanation.walkthrough: ETOMER, in offensivE TO ME Rebuff, reads upwards. 'Slight' looks like a snub but means small.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote chance is a slight one: faint, unlikely.

clue.text: Dimpled skin left on primate with sword

indicators.note: the letter for left goes on, tacked after the other pieces

parts.note: orang is short for orang-utan, a great ape
an épée is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: An ape with a sword leaves pockmarked skin behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange peel is the dimpled rind of the fruit, also a name for dimpled human skin.

clue.text: Old soldiers behind walls in Germany, I say!

indicators.note: to wall something in is to enclose it, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: rear means behind
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
my is an exclamation like I say!

explanation.surface: Veterans stuck behind the walls of a German town provoke an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Army was the Soviet army, so its troops are soldiers of a former era.

clue.text: Duck with two functions?

parts.note: a do is a function in the sense of a party, and a use is a function in the sense of a purpose, so two functions together make a word meaning to duck

explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to plunge them into water, and to douse is to drench or plunge.

clue.text: Old maestro taking cap off hole in device filming workers?

indicators.note: the device takes a letter in, holding it inside

parts.note: worker bees are filmed by a bee cam, a camera on a hive

indicators.note: the cap off a word is its top, so its first letter

explanation.surface: A conductor doffs his cap to fix a hole in a camera spying on workers.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes into BEECAM. Sir Thomas Beecham was a famous British conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas Beecham was a celebrated British conductor of the last century, an old maestro.

clue.text: Tired little dog eating article up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from the bottom, backwards
the dog eating something holds it inside

parts.note: a lab is short for Labrador, the dog's name made little
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A weary pup chews up a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: LAB eating AN gives LANAB, which reads upwards. 'Tired' means hackneyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired ideas are stale and hackneyed, which is what banal means.

clue.text: I poop on teacher, old fossil?

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece placed on another comes before it here, sitting on top

parts.note: guano is the droppings of seabirds or bats
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A pupil confesses to an outrageous prank on an aged schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old fossil' looks like an insult for the teacher, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon is a dinosaur known from fossil remains, so literally an old fossil.

clue.text: Maladroit fiance spat regularly

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of these words, starting with the second

explanation.surface: An awkward husband-to-be keeps having rows.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone clumsy or lacking skill.

clue.text: Comic actor with Queen frequenting shops where goldfish bought?

indicators.note: to frequent a place is to be in it often, so the Queen goes inside

parts.note: goldfish are bought at pet shops, run by pet sellers
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A comedian goes with the Queen to shop for a goldfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Sellers was the English comedian and film actor of The Pink Panther and The Goon Show.
